findings.text: follow-on: `assert set(family["members"]) == {m["id"] for m in _MEMBERS}` compares the report's member list against _MEMBERS, the exact fixture the test handed the stub, which returns that same list, so it holds whatever the report's family enumeration does; the count assertions at :130 and :167 have the same shape. The assertion that does bite is tests/standard_names/test_harmonize.py:531 (`assert shared in issued`), which fails if build_worklist re-inlines the grouping.

follow-on: the node adds Cypher (the pattern-family enumeration) but its recorded after_suite omits tests/graph/test_cypher_property_check.py and the review/audits tests that the node's own done_when names as gate files, so the recorded gate does not assert property existence for the new literals; I ran the property check at 3ec6cfb25 and it passes (4 passed, EXIT=0), so no defect shipped, but the record is incomplete against the done_when.

follow-on: report_family_rows keys lint findings by finding.name_id into by_name at :647, then attributes them per family via by_name.get(member id) at :659; run_lexical_lint emits its cross-name position-form findings under the synthetic id `[domain:<d>]` (imas_codex/standard_names/review/audits.py:387) which matches no member id, so those findings are dropped from every family row and from the scope total the plan calls the number every later step is judged against.

follow-on: fetch_pattern_families reuses families.py's primitives (_invariant_projection/_invariant_equality/PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS) but its seeded branch re-derives the invariant grouping families.py already owns in _PATTERN_FAMILY_MEMBERS_QUERY/fetch_pattern_family (imas_codex/standard_names/families.py:547,605), and the bulk form places a family-enumeration capability in harmonize.py rather than beside that owner; it extends rather than forks the primitives, so it is not a full duplicate, but the multi-seed and all-families forms belong in the module that owns family enumeration.
